chapter_title: Chương 72: Báo chí đưa tin, toàn Xuyên đều biết tiếng

segments.title: Chương 72: Báo chí đưa tin, toàn Xuyên đều biết tiếng
segments.content:
Three-quarters of the class had already heard the news in advance.

The vast majority of them had heard about it in the last hour or two. Xu Haibo, Xie Yang, and others were spreading it everywhere, and Chen Guiliang had to patiently deal with another wave of them.

Only someone like Li Jun, who arrived at school right on time, would need to get the information from the head teacher.

The head teacher, Liu Shuying, praised Chen Guiliang profusely, then admonished the other students: "Chen Guiliang being specially recruited by a prestigious university is an extremely rare special case. He has always enjoyed reading extracurricular books and has a long-term accumulation of literary knowledge, which is why he could achieve such stunning success. It's too late for you to learn from him now, so you should focus on the college entrance exam and seriously review the key concepts..."

"Now, I will announce the final exam results. The questions on the final exams for each subject were harder than on the monthly exam, so the admission score lines have also been set lower..."

"Wu Meng, total score 661, first in the grade. Second in the entire city!"

"Li Rui, total score 654, second in the grade. Fourth in the entire city!"

For those not in the city's top thirty, Liu Shuying didn't bother announcing their city-wide ranking.

For those ranked outside the school's top one hundred, she couldn't even be bothered to read their names out, directly asking Li Rui to distribute the report cards.

When Chen Guiliang got his report card, he was quite satisfied with his performance.

Chinese: 138, Math: 81, English: 95, Liberal Arts Comprehensive: 242.

Total score: 556.

The Tier 1 university admission score line was 550.

His math score was a particularly pleasant surprise. The monthly exam questions had been very simple, and he had only scored 68. The final exam questions were much harder, yet he actually scored an 81, which showed that his review had been very effective.

Although his English score had only increased by 2 points from the monthly exam, the questions were harder, so it was also a sign of steady improvement.

And then there was his total score.

On the monthly exam, Chen Guiliang had just barely passed the Tier 2 university admission score line by 1 point.

On the final exam, Chen Guiliang had surpassed the Tier 1 university admission score line by 6 points!

His scores in Chinese and Liberal Arts Comprehensive were pulling his average up so drastically that as long as his Math and English were somewhat decent, he could get into a Tier 1 university.

Liu Shuying now found Chen Guiliang more and more pleasing to the eye. She even offered a couple of special words of praise: "Although Chen Guiliang was distracted preparing for the composition competition, his hard work last semester was there for all to see. Even without a prestigious university specially recruiting him, he could have gotten into a Tier 1 university on his own merits. Let's give him a round of applause!"

A wave of applause erupted, with Bian Guanyue and Xu Haibo clapping the most enthusiastically.

Last Christmas Eve, Zheng Feng had already given up on pursuing Bian Guanyue and had thrown himself into his studies.

At this moment, Zheng Feng was completely convinced, clearly recognizing the gap between himself and Chen Guiliang.

He turned his head to look at Chen Guiliang, with only a sigh left in his heart.

No more fighting, no more competing. There are plenty of other fish in the sea.

"As I said last semester, we will be changing seats again after the final exams. This time, in order from the highest score to the lowest, students can choose for themselves..."

Wu Meng chose to stay where she was. She wasn't tall, so sitting in the first row was fine, and it was convenient for asking the teacher questions.

Li Rui, however, chose to sit in the middle of the second row, right behind Wu Meng. Here, you didn't have to breathe in chalk dust, nor did you have to crane your neck to listen to the lecture, and you could also discuss difficult problems with Wu Meng.

The middle seats in the second, third, and fourth rows were quickly snatched up by the top students.

When it was Chen Guiliang's turn, he couldn't be bothered to move again. The second-to-last row was perfectly fine.

Bian Guanyue didn't move either. No one was fighting with her for a spot in the first row, and it was perfect for continuing to sit with her good friend Wu Meng. She actually wanted to be deskmates with Chen Guiliang, but she was too shy to say it out loud.

In terms of study attitude alone, Bian Guanyue was far more diligent than Chen Guiliang, working her hardest to make up for the lessons she missed as an art student.

Her final exam score was still in the Tier 3 range, but she was only 4 points away from the Tier 2 university admission line.

After the seats were rearranged, Liu Shuying smiled and waved. "Chen Guiliang, come here for a moment, and bring a stool with you."

In the past, when Chen Guiliang was called over by the head teacher for a talk, it was usually a private chat in the hallway or the office.

But now, he was sitting next to the teacher's desk, with no need to avoid prying eyes.

"Have you decided which university to attend?" Liu Shuying asked.

The students in the first few rows immediately pricked up their ears.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm waiting for news from Qinghua and Peking University. If that doesn't work out, I'll choose Fudan."

Those words were practically asking for a punch. The students in the front row were rendered speechless.

Liu Shuying asked again, "Is there anything you need the school to do?"

Chen Guiliang said, "The special recruitment from the New Concept Competition goes through the universities' independent admission process. I have to take the independent admission exam in March and also provide personal materials to the university. These materials need the school's official stamp."

"List out what materials you need, and I'll help you get them ready," Liu Shuying said.

"Thank you, Teacher Liu," Chen Guiliang said.

Liu Shuying added, "The school leadership has discussed it and decided to invite some media outlets for publicity. We'll need your cooperation then. Your demerits have all been rescinded, understand?"

"Understood," Chen Guiliang said.

Principal Yan had planned to invite twenty to thirty media outlets, but unfortunately, the school didn't have enough clout, and Chen Guiliang didn't carry enough weight.

In this situation, you couldn't even pay to get them to come.

The main reason was that this backwater county town was too remote, and reporters from major coastal newspapers were unwilling to waste their time.

Principal Yan personally contacted dozens of media outlets, and so far, only seven or eight had agreed to grace them with their presence, with half of them being Sichuan-based publications.

If it were to promote Guo Xiaosi, many more reporters would surely be willing to come. But Guo Xiaosi was busy lately, occupied with starting his own company. He had already scheduled his return to his alma mater for the second half of the year.

Unless Chen Guiliang's topic heat continued to rise, then reporters would come uninvited.

This would require a trigger.

For example, when Han Han wrote "Viewing People in a Cup," it did indeed spark a nationwide discussion, but it was like a gust of wind that passed, and the heat died down very quickly. What truly ignited public opinion was Han Han flunking his courses and dropping out of school!

And by taking advantage of flunking and dropping out, he also published "Triple Gate," and the novel's sales finally reached their peak.

The eighteenth day of the first lunar month.

A new issue of the West China Metropolis Daily was out.

For six consecutive years, this newspaper had ranked among the world's top 100 daily newspapers by circulation.

Its current average daily circulation was 1.1 million copies, mainly distributed in the Sichuan-Chongqing region.

Not only did government and public institutions throughout Sichuan subscribe to it automatically, but ordinary people also liked to read it. You could buy a copy at any newsstand.

Xiao Weidong was an ordinary small business owner who ran a photo studio in Rongcheng.

His main income came from taking ID photos, but he also offered typing and copying services, and sold newspapers and magazines on the side.

A comprehensive business model.

In reality, the shop was very small. Besides himself, he only had one young apprentice.

The photo studio was located in an old alley, and every day, neighbors would come over to sit for a while, taking the opportunity to read the newspapers he sold for free.

"Boss Xiao, business is good, eh?"

"Good my ass. I've only had two photo customers all morning. You want to get a picture taken?"

"You've already taken my damn funeral portrait, what other picture do I need?"

This old neighbor swaggered into the shop, moved a stool, and then sat at the entrance, reading a newspaper for free.

Xiao Weidong teased, "You're sure taking it easy. You want me to make you a cup of tea, too?"

"That'd be fine. Thanks for the trouble," the old neighbor laughed.

The old neighbor was reading the West China Metropolis Daily, which was the first choice for the citizens of Rongcheng.

Suddenly, a customer came to get an ID photo taken and to copy their ID card. Xiao Weidong had his apprentice handle it, while he himself lay down in the shade of a tree to doze off.

Before long, he heard the neighbor say, "Whoa, this student is really something else!"

Xiao Weidong asked, "Something else how?"

"He wrote an essay and got recommended to Qinghua and Peking University. And something about composing a poem in seven steps. Dared to stand up to the triads when he was in junior high."

"You believe that kind of bragging?"

"See for yourself."

Xiao Weidong went over to take a look, then picked up another copy of the West China Metropolis Daily and flipped directly to the Culture and Entertainment section.

The headline on the culture page was striking: A Modern-Day 'Poem in Seven Steps'—Exploring the Growth of a Teenage Literary Genius.

"In mid-January of this year, at the Qingsongcheng Hotel, famous figures were gathered, and the media had assembled. Dong Hongkang, a senior editor from the Wenhui Daily, gave four keywords and demanded that Chen Guiliang, a third-year high school student, compose a classical poem on the spot. Why would a distinguished and well-known editor make things difficult for a high school student?"

"The story goes back to the day before. The 6th National New Concept Composition Competition was held as scheduled. Chen Guiliang, a student from Fushi No. 2 High School in Longdu City, astounded the judging committee with his piece 'Ying Hai Xing'. Mr. Wang Meng, the former Minister of Culture, gave 'Ying Hai Xing' high praise and held a seminar to analyze and appreciate it in detail. Major universities, including Qinghua and Peking University, vied to specially recruit Chen Guiliang, even to the point of fighting over him."

"The preface and poem of 'Ying Hai Xing' were written entirely in classical Chinese. Moreover, the writing was sophisticated, the imagination bizarre, the momentum majestic, and the theme lofty. This did not seem like something a high school student could write. The editor from Wenhui Daily raised doubts about this and tested him on the spot. Chen Guiliang picked up a calligraphy brush, and after walking seven steps, he wrote a high-quality five-character quatrain. Editor Dong Hongkang praised him repeatedly and took the original manuscript of the poem for his collection."

"How could a high school student from a small county town have such a profound foundation in classical Chinese? With this question in mind, this reporter visited Chen Guiliang's junior high and high school alma maters..."

The rest of the article was interspersed with interviews with Chen Guiliang's junior high and high school teachers, as well as interviews from the local police station and vendors at the township market.

Even Chen Guiliang's elementary school was mentioned, because the vice-principal of his junior high often visited the various village elementary schools in the countryside.

A left-behind child in a poor rural village, who had no extracurricular books to read as a child, could only memorize textbooks and the dictionary.

In junior high, he bravely fought against local evil forces, leading to the arrest and sentencing of the gang leader, and he also achieved first place in the entire town in his high school entrance exam.

In high school, he scrimped and saved, going hungry to buy books, his academic performance never slipping, and went alone to Modu to achieve stunning success!

"So, what do you think?" the old neighbor asked.

Xiao Weidong said, "Badass. That's seriously awesome!"

"What are you guys talking about?" Another neighbor came over to get a free read of the paper.

Xiao Weidong handed him the West China Metropolis Daily. "A Sichuan kid. He's really fierce, skilled in both letters and arms."

After that neighbor finished reading the article, he actually took out money to buy the newspaper.

Xiao Weidong laughed, "You're feeling generous today, eh? Willing to part with your money."

The neighbor said, "I'm buying it to take home. I'll show it to my grandson when he gets out of school. Other people's kids are so well-behaved, but all he knows how to do is play around all day long."

"Just give him a few more beatings."

"Beating doesn't work on him."

The first old neighbor said, "This kid, Chen Guiliang, is truly impressive. You can't just teach someone to be like that. He's a left-behind child with no one at home to supervise him; it's all self-discipline. He's got a sharp mind. In ancient times, he would definitely have passed the county-level imperial exam."

"What county-level exam? He'd pass the highest imperial exam!"

"Nearsighted? Does he need glasses too?"

"You don't know a damn thing!"

"..."

This time, Chen Guiliang had truly become famous, at least especially famous in Rongcheng.

This was because in Rongcheng alone, the West China Metropolis Daily sold over 700,000 copies, and often, many people would share a single newspaper.

A daily newspaper reporter from Longdu City, catching on late, drove to the school the next day, becoming the second person to conduct an on-site interview.

As for his situation at No. 2 High School, Chen Guiliang had already become a legendary figure.

He had perplexingly received a number of love letters from younger female students.

(Thanks to big boss Bùrú Qù Chīfàn for the Alliance Lord donation.)
